title: Prognostic Value of Tau-SAA as a Biomarker for the Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease
summary:
Today's tests for Alzheimer's dementia—whether in cerebrospinal fluid, blood, or through imaging—very often yield positive results even though the subjects do not develop the disease. This means that existing screening tests are not of sufficient quality and are therefore of limited use.
A new technology from SeNostic makes a new biomarker available for detecting the tau protein in the blood. The single-arm, prospective, observational, clinical correlation study described here aims to investigate, for the first time, the correlation between the detected protein (tau-SAA) and the severity of Alzheimer's symptoms.
The study aims to measure tau-SAA and p-tau217 levels in the blood of patients diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease who have undergone cerebrospinal fluid analysis. In addition, clinical data and the routinely administered Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) will be correlated with the laboratory data.
As many patients as possible with a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s dementia who are scheduled for a routine blood draw will be recruited for the study.
No additional invasive tests will be performed for the study. Routinely collected medical history data, demographic data, clinical data, a cognitive test (Montreal Cognitive Assessment), and routinely performed laboratory tests will be documented.
A cerebrospinal fluid analysis for the diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease must be documented in the medical history, and the data must be submitted. No repeat cerebrospinal fluid  analysis will be performed.
In addition to the standard laboratory tests, tau-SAA and p-tau217 levels will be measured in the blood.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients aged 18 and older
• Gender: men and women
• Signed informed consent form
• Indication for routine blood draw
• Confirmed diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease
• One-third of patients each with mild (MoCA 18–25), moderate (MoCA 10–17), and severe (MoCA <10) disease severity
Exclusion criteria:
• Presence of myopathy
• Family relationship with the trial site or the sponsor
• Prisoners
• Alcohol or drug abuse
